Alright, so I have this English statement about a theorem in Euclidean geometry, and I need to formalize it using Lean 4. The statement is: "In any triangle, the greater side subtends the greater angle. For let $ABC$ be a triangle having side $AC$ greater than $AB$. I say that angle $ABC$ is also greater than $BCA$." 

Okay, first, I need to understand what this means. In a triangle, if one side is longer than another, the angle opposite the longer side is larger. So, in triangle $ABC$, if $AC > AB$, then angle $ABC$ (which is opposite $AC$) is greater than angle $BCA$ (which is opposite $AB$).

Now, I need to translate this into Lean 4 code. I've seen some examples, so I know I need to start with `theorem theorem_name (h1 : hypothesis_1) (h2 : hypothesis_2) ... : conclusion := by

reference_formalization: ∀ (a b c : Point) (AB BC AC : Line), formTriangle a b c AB BC AC ∧ (|(a─c)| > |(a─b)|) → (∠ a:b:c > ∠ b:c:a)
nl_statement: In any triangle, the greater side subtends the greater angle. For let $ABC$ be a triangle having side $AC$ greater than $AB$. I say that angle $ABC$ is also greater than $BCA$.   <prf>  Thus, $ABC$ is much greater than  $ACB$.  Thus, in any triangle, the greater side subtends the greater angle. (Which is) the very thing  it was required to show.
